memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: So when God destroyed the cities of the plain, he remembered Abraham, and he brought Lot out of the catastrophe that overthrew the cities where Lot had lived. - Gen 19:29 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Here is the key that unlocks the whole chapter: "God remembered Abraham, and he brought Lot out." Why was Lot rescued? Not because Lot was so faithful - we've seen his many failures. He was saved because God remembered Abraham. Lot was spared through his connection to a man who stood in the gap for him. He was rescued on account of another.

This is a beautiful and important truth. Lot's salvation flowed not from his own merit but through his relationship to Abraham, whose intercession moved the heart of God. Our prayers for others matter more than we know. Abraham's pleading, offered the day before, became the reason Lot lived.

Think of the people connected to you whom God may bless because of your faithfulness and prayers. A godly grandmother's prayers, a faithful friend's intercession, a parent's tears before God - these are not forgotten. God remembers. Our intercession weaves a net of grace around those we love.

And this points to the deepest truth of the gospel. We too are saved not by our own merit but on account of Another - Jesus Christ, who "always lives to intercede" for us (Heb 7:25). As Lot was rescued because God remembered Abraham, so we are rescued because God remembers His Son and all that He accomplished for us. Our whole salvation rests on being connected to Christ. In Him, God remembers us with saving mercy.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Are you interceding for those God has connected to your life?
- Do you rest in being saved on account of Christ, not your own merit?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Lord, thank You that You remember. Thank You that I am saved not by my own merit but on account of Christ, my Intercessor. Help me faithfully pray for those You have connected to my life.
Amen.
